"""One of the eight axis-aligned symmetries, uniformly.

    Z, Y and X are each flipped independently with probability 0.5, so the identity is
    one of eight equally likely outcomes rather than a special case.

    **Z is included.** This repository's TTA modes exclude the Z flip on the reasoning
    that it is out of distribution at 4x coarser Z sampling; the recipe the checkpoints
    were trained under says otherwise, and `frontier_plus_flip3d` is the arm that prices
    the same correction at inference time.

    ``coords`` is cloned rather than flipped in place -- the dataset hands out tensors it
    keeps, and mutating them would corrupt the window for every later epoch. Padded
    slots stay at zero: only positions under ``masks`` are reflected, so a coordinate
    that means "no node here" is not turned into one at the far edge of the volume.
    """
    flip_mask = rng.random(3) < 0.5  # (Z, Y, X)
    dims_to_flip = [1 + dim for dim, flip in enumerate(flip_mask) if flip]
    if not dims_to_flip:
        return imgs, coords, masks

    imgs = imgs.flip(dims=dims_to_flip)

    coords = coords.clone()
    shape = imgs.shape[1:]  # (Z, Y, X) of the downsampled volume
    for dim in range(3):
        if flip_mask[dim]:
            axis = coords[..., dim]
            axis[masks] = shape[dim] - axis[masks] - 1
            coords[..., dim] = axis
    return imgs, coords, masks

Why the selection is a proven optimum for each class, not a greedy repair
------------------------------------------------------------------------
Nodes and coordinates are frozen, so the official node matching is fixed. The matching
is one-to-one, so each GT edge has at most one candidate predicted edge, so a predicted
edge's TP / FP / ignored status depends only on its own endpoints. The protected
division closure keeps every fork's scored neighbourhood identical, so the division
term is constant (checked by the official scorer, not assumed). The aggregate adjusted

maximised exactly by Dinkelbach iteration: for fixed lambda, maximise
``sum f_i TP - lambda FP``, which separates into one exact assignment problem per
frame boundary (``solve_boundary``). Iterate lambda to its fixed point. The additivity
assumption is checked: per-movie TP/FP recomputed from pair statuses must equal the
official scorer's counts for both base and edited outputs.
